blocks.md: This lesson follows **The Delegation Trade-Off** in *Multi-Agent Coordination* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, Multi-Agent Coordination, § The Delegation Trade-Off
blocks.md: Handing the interface update and the caller update to dedicated workers differs from issuing concurrent model queries, and that difference defines the unit of delegation. A **delegated worker** owns a bounded child trajectory with its own context window, model-and-tool loop, task contract, and independent lifecycle. Several candidate samples dispatched by one controller, such as the self-consistency votes of test-time compute, are instead parallel calls inside one trajectory.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Coordination overhead matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Under Speedup(N) = 1/((1-p) + p/N + c(N)) any gain requires c(N) < p(1 - 1/N), the best count sits near sqrt(p/c) for linear overhead, and the serial fraction caps speedup at 1/(1-p).

questions.q: The section **The Delegation Trade-Off** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A credit window enforces free plus outstanding equal to W, bounding in-flight payload and, by Little's law, mean staleness at W/mu, which per-agent token budgets cannot do.

Shared working directories produce lost updates and torn reads, and write sets collide with probability 1 - exp(-N(N-1)w^2/2F), so isolation is provided per worker and a merge is validated, not trusted.

For a fixed amount of work with no coordination overhead, the serial fraction 1-p caps speedup at 1/(1-p) however many workers are added, and the universal scalability law reduces to it when coherency is zero.
Under Speedup(N) = 1/((1-p) + p/N + c(N)) any gain requires c(N) < p(1 - 1/N), the best count sits near sqrt(p/c) for linear overhead, and the serial fraction caps speedup at 1/(1-p).

questions.q: True or false: in the book's concept map, *Coordination overhead* adds coordination cost to *Harness owns continuation*.
questions.hint: Which later concept does this idea actually connect to?
questions.explanation: False. The book links *Coordination overhead* adds coordination cost to *Critical-path acceleration ceiling*.
